# SPEC 2.2 uses "walk" as its own normative term (Rule A6). The specification is frozen and these lines stay.
# The two Satoshi Hike 2.0 allowlist entries named a file this tree no longer has.
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	**Asynchronous model.** The walk is the back-to-back run of legs from the seed to the final interrupt. Every waypoint post, Hashcash solve, path ask, peer or header-source read, Bari exchange, and log write is an asynchronous event. None of them pauses a leg (Rule A6). The one read on the walk path is the tip read after each checkpoint, and it never waits. A run ends only at the final interrupt, on a producer failure, or on explicit cancellation.
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	| P9.12 | INVARIANT | No clock-read failure or other transitory network condition stops a run or withholds the object. Produce logs it (section 13.5) and the walk continues. An unsuccessful Hashcash, POST, or path-ask read is a miss, and produce continues. A run ends only at `I_17`, on a producer failure, or on explicit cancellation. | §9, Rule A6 |
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	| P9.16 | CONSTANT | On the live plane the header source keeps at least `HEADER_PEERS_MIN` 2 gossip peers. A connected peer that has not announced a header within `HEADER_PEER_SILENCE_SECONDS` 120 of another connected peer announcing it is replaced. Below 2 peers the source reconnects asynchronously with backoff and writes an `alert` `header_peers_low`; the walk and the object are unaffected. | §9 |
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	| A6 | INVARIANT | No post, Hashcash solve, ask, peer or header-source read, Bari exchange, or log write pauses, orders, delays, or interrupts a leg. Each is an asynchronous event. The post-checkpoint tip read stays on the walk path and never waits. | §13 Rule A6 |
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	| Asynchronous event | Work the producer starts and does not wait for on the walk path: a post, a solve, an ask, a header-source or peer read, a Bari exchange, or a log write (Rule A6). |
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	| walk or re-walk, for a leg | leg, or recomputed leg result |
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	**Header source.** On the live plane the producer’s header source keeps sessions with at least `HEADER_PEERS_MIN` gossip peers at the same time, for the whole run. `HEADER_PEERS_MIN` is 2. A peer announces a header when it relays that header or a header that builds on it. When one connected peer has announced a header and another connected peer has not announced it within `HEADER_PEER_SILENCE_SECONDS` of the first announcement, the silent peer is disconnected and replaced by a new peer from the starting list or from addresses that peers have given. `HEADER_PEER_SILENCE_SECONDS` is 120. Both values are constants of this file. They are not levers and not SDK options. While no peer announces a new header, no peer is replaced: a natural gap between blocks is not silence. When fewer than `HEADER_PEERS_MIN` peers are connected, the header source keeps connecting new peers asynchronously, backing off between attempts, and writes an `alert` record (section 13.5) named `header_peers_low` each time the count falls below `HEADER_PEERS_MIN`. The walk continues, the object is unaffected, and the run still follows this section. A header source built to use one peer does not follow this section. Keeping, replacing, and reconnecting peers is asynchronous work and never pauses a leg (Rule A6). The copied list is checked again against Bitcoin Core's mainnet chainparams when a producer release is cut.
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	A clock read that does not succeed never stops the run and never withholds the object. A post-checkpoint tip read that does not succeed is not an interrupt: the walk continues with its next leg, and produce logs the transitory condition (section 13.5). An Observe for the fee header, a waypoint POST, or a path ask that does not succeed is a miss. Rule A3.4 records it and produce continues.
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	**Normative.** The walk is the back-to-back run of legs from the seed through `I_17`. Every waypoint post, Hashcash solve, path ask, peer or header-source read, Bari exchange, event-log write, and stderr write is an asynchronous event. No such event pauses, delays, orders, or interrupts a leg, and no leg waits for one to finish. The only read on the walk path is the post-checkpoint tip read (Rule A1.1), which returns at once the latest header the header source already holds. A failed read, a stalled header source, a Bari outage, a log that cannot be written, a slow peer, or any other transitory network condition is logged (section 13.5), and the walk continues. A run ends only at `I_17`, on a producer failure, or on explicit cancellation. Bugs are producer failures; they are not covered by this rule. Asynchronous work may share the host’s CPU with legs. This rule does not change what a leg computes, and it does not permit any change to the terrain, the step, the fold, or the slot read.
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	**Fee header.** When the post of `W_g` starts, the producer takes as fee header the 80-byte block header its header source holds as best tip. Its `header_hash` is `SHA-256(SHA-256(header))`, 32 bytes in natural order. Taking it is not a tip read of the walk, does not end a stage, and is not `I_g`. If the header source holds no header, the POST does not succeed: produce logs the miss and continues.
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	6. **Alert.** When the run meets a transitory condition that does not stop it, for example a tip read that did not succeed, a header-source stall, a fee header that is not available, or a log append that did not succeed (written when appending works again, if it does). `event` is `hike.produce.alert`. `alert` is a short lowercase name of the condition, for example `clock_read_failed`, `header_source_stalled`, `fee_header_missing`, or `log_append_failed`. `stage` is the stage the walk was in. `height` is the height concerned, and is omitted when there is none. An alert is not an input to the hike and does not change the object.
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	**Measuring method.** Measure on an owned commodity host. The low end of that set is the low-end owned host (an Intel Core i7-10610U laptop, no SHA-NI). Use a conforming SDK at the cut tag of this file (section 16.2) that passes the whole pack, including every permanent negative. Run a real beacon-paced hike under this file’s producer rules: nothing pauses a leg (Rule A6), and there is no wait before a path ask. The rate is the first-beacon to last-beacon rate, `hike_legs / hike_span`, Rule A4.10, with `hike_span` the median-time-past difference. The floor is calibrated on the best legal packed rate per machine. That rate is `N` parallel PCOCs with distinct keys. Distinct keys make distinct terrains under this seed. An interleave of those hikes is the packed rate. Shared-terrain packing across distinct PCOCs is impossible under this seed. It is not a legal schedule. Record the host, the CPU, the implementation, the commit, and that packed rate beside the single-hike rate. A policy that follows this method sets the floor a little below the low-end host’s rate. **The floor must be measured under this file.** A rate measured with a producer that paused the walk (for example, with a wait before path asks or a blocking post) is not a measurement for this file: those pauses sat inside `hike_span` and understate the rate a producer of this file reaches at the same cost per leg. This method informs the value a policy sets. It does not set one.
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	An SDK producer runs the walk on its own thread or threads and runs every post, solve, ask, header-source read, Bari exchange, and log write as asynchronous work (Rule A6). The walk reads the tip through a call that returns at once. No SDK producer sleeps, waits on I/O, takes a lock that I/O holds, or syncs a file on the walk path. A failure of asynchronous work becomes an `alert` record or a logged miss; it never propagates into the walk. Only a producer failure or explicit cancellation ends a run before `I_17`. The header source detects a stalled or lagging peer and recovers on its own, asynchronously; a stall never pauses a leg.
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	| F5 | Waypoint post before the next stage’s legs (blocking post). | The walk waited on Bari and on the Hashcash solve, so legs paused at every boundary and the measured rate fell. | Rule A1.4 (post is asynchronous); Rule A6; Rule I3. |
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	| F6 | The 15–45 s wait before each path ask. | It ran inside the walk and cost about 1,000 s per hike (7.6–8 %). Rates and the floor measured with it understate an honest producer. | Section 13.1 (an ask is sent when due, with no wait); P13.7; Rule A6; section 15.5 (re-measure the floor). |
# SPEC 2.3 is 2.2 plus clarifications and keeps "walk" as its own normative term (Rule A6: the back-to-back run of legs).
# Same 15 lines as 2.2; they differ only by inline anchors and, for the section 15.5 Measuring method, the 2.3 D5 sentences.
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.3/SPEC.md	**Asynchronous model.** The walk is the back-to-back run of legs from the seed to the final interrupt. Every waypoint post, Hashcash solve, path ask, peer or header-source read, Bari exchange, and log write is an asynchronous event. None of them pauses a leg (Rule A6). The one read on the walk path is the tip read after each checkpoint, and it never waits. A run ends only at the final interrupt, on a producer failure, or on explicit cancellation.

spec/satoshi-hike-v2.3/SPEC.md	**Header source.** On the live plane the producer’s header source keeps sessions with at least `HEADER_PEERS_MIN` gossip peers at the same time, for the whole run. `HEADER_PEERS_MIN` is 2. A peer announces a header when it relays that header or a header that builds on it. When one connected peer has announced a header and another connected peer has not announced it within `HEADER_PEER_SILENCE_SECONDS` of the first announcement, the silent peer is disconnected and replaced by a new peer from the starting list or from addresses that peers have given. `HEADER_PEER_SILENCE_SECONDS` is 120. Both values are constants of this file. They are not levers and not SDK options. While no peer announces a new header, no peer is replaced: a natural gap between blocks is not silence. When fewer than `HEADER_PEERS_MIN` peers are connected, the header source keeps connecting new peers asynchronously, backing off between attempts, and writes an `alert` record (section 13.5) named `header_peers_low` each time the count falls below `HEADER_PEERS_MIN`. The walk continues, the object is unaffected, and the run still follows this section. A header source built to use one peer does not follow this section. Keeping, replacing, and reconnecting peers is asynchronous work and never pauses a leg (Rule A6). The copied list is checked again against Bitcoin Core's mainnet chainparams when a producer release is cut.
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.3/SPEC.md	A clock read that does not succeed never stops the run and never withholds the object. A post-checkpoint tip read that does not succeed is not an interrupt: the walk continues with its next leg, and produce logs the transitory condition (section 13.5). An Observe for the fee header, a waypoint POST, or a path ask that does not succeed is a miss. Rule A3.4 records it and produce continues.
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.3/SPEC.md	**Normative.** The walk is the back-to-back run of legs from the seed through `I_17`. Every waypoint post, Hashcash solve, path ask, peer or header-source read, Bari exchange, event-log write, and stderr write is an asynchronous event. No such event pauses, delays, orders, or interrupts a leg, and no leg waits for one to finish. The only read on the walk path is the post-checkpoint tip read (Rule A1.1), which returns at once the latest header the header source already holds. A failed read, a stalled header source, a Bari outage, a log that cannot be written, a slow peer, or any other transitory network condition is logged (section 13.5), and the walk continues. A run ends only at `I_17`, on a producer failure, or on explicit cancellation. Bugs are producer failures; they are not covered by this rule. Asynchronous work may share the host’s CPU with legs. This rule does not change what a leg computes, and it does not permit any change to the terrain, the step, the fold, or the slot read.
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.3/SPEC.md	**Fee header.** When the post of `W_g` starts, the producer takes as fee header the 80-byte block header its header source holds as best tip. Its `header_hash` is `SHA-256(SHA-256(header))`, 32 bytes in natural order. Taking it is not a tip read of the walk, does not end a stage, and is not `I_g`. If the header source holds no header, the POST does not succeed: produce logs the miss and continues.
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.3/SPEC.md	6. **Alert.** When the run meets a transitory condition that does not stop it, for example a tip read that did not succeed, a header-source stall, a fee header that is not available, or a log append that did not succeed (written when appending works again, if it does). `event` is `hike.produce.alert`. `alert` is a short lowercase name of the condition, for example `clock_read_failed`, `header_source_stalled`, `fee_header_missing`, or `log_append_failed`. `stage` is the stage the walk was in. `height` is the height concerned, and is omitted when there is none. An alert is not an input to the hike and does not change the object.
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.3/SPEC.md	**Measuring method.** Measure on an owned commodity host. The low end of that set is the low-end owned host (an Intel Core i7-10610U laptop, no SHA-NI). Use a conforming SDK at the cut tag of this file (section 16.2) that passes the whole pack, including every permanent negative. Use the fastest such producer build available for that host, and record with the rate whether its fold ran vectorised or scalar and whether its SHA-256 ran in hardware or software. Run a real beacon-paced hike under this file’s producer rules: nothing pauses a leg (Rule A6), and there is no wait before a path ask. The rate is the first-beacon to last-beacon rate, `hike_legs / hike_span`, Rule A4.10, with `hike_span` the median-time-past difference. The floor is calibrated on the best legal packed rate per machine. That rate is `N` parallel PCOCs with distinct keys. Distinct keys make distinct terrains under this seed. An interleave of those hikes is the packed rate. Shared-terrain packing across distinct PCOCs is impossible under this seed. It is not a legal schedule. Record the host, the CPU, the implementation, the commit, and that packed rate beside the single-hike rate. A policy that follows this method sets the floor a little below the low-end host’s rate. It does not set the floor above the rate that the released conforming SDKs reach on the low-end host. That constraint binds whoever sets or raises the floor. It is not a comparison the admission service makes. **The floor must be measured under this file.** A rate measured with a producer that paused the walk (for example, with a wait before path asks or a blocking post) is not a measurement for this file: those pauses sat inside `hike_span` and understate the rate a producer of this file reaches at the same cost per leg. This method informs the value a policy sets. It does not set one.
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.3/SPEC.md	An SDK producer runs the walk on its own thread or threads and runs every post, solve, ask, header-source read, Bari exchange, and log write as asynchronous work (Rule A6). The walk reads the tip through a call that returns at once. No SDK producer sleeps, waits on I/O, takes a lock that I/O holds, or syncs a file on the walk path. A failure of asynchronous work becomes an `alert` record or a logged miss; it never propagates into the walk. Only a producer failure or explicit cancellation ends a run before `I_17`. The header source detects a stalled or lagging peer and recovers on its own, asynchronously; a stall never pauses a leg.

# Unedited builder reports in spec/conformance/interop. Reviewed 23 Oct 2026:
# these four lines use "walk" as the specification's own term (walk time, walk a leg).
# Exact line match only. Any edit of the line is a hit again.
spec/conformance/interop/round-2/D-gemini-kotlin/RESULTS.md	### Flaw 1: Unbound `last_interrupt` (`I_17`) and unanchored `W_17` grant `K` extra blocks of walk time outside `hike_span` (saves 14.3%–25.0% required leg rate)
spec/conformance/interop/round-2/D-gemini-kotlin/RESULTS.md	  4. Furthermore, §15.5 (line 2054) assumes that a single PCOC's legs are strictly sequential so that using `C` CPU cores requires running `C` distinct PCOCs with `C × 256 MiB` of separate terrains. Because a fake leg takes 0 steps to produce a valid `checkpoints[j]` reset point, an attacker with `C` cores sharing **one** 256 MiB terrain can insert `C - 1` fake legs in a long hike of `L` legs and compute the remaining `L - (C - 1)` honest legs **in parallel across all `C` cores**. For example, in a 2,000-leg hike on an 8-core machine, inserting 7 fake legs (`0.35%` fake fraction) lets all 8 cores walk honest legs in parallel on a single 256 MiB terrain while passing an 18-leg thorough draw `(1 - 7/2000)^18 = 93.9%` of the time (or `97.9%` of the time for §14 standalone `verify`, which only ever checks 6 legs).
spec/conformance/interop/round-2/D-gemini-kotlin/code/RESULTS.md	### Flaw 1: Unbound `last_interrupt` (`I_17`) and unanchored `W_17` grant `K` extra blocks of walk time outside `hike_span` (saves 14.3%–25.0% required leg rate)
spec/conformance/interop/round-2/D-gemini-kotlin/code/RESULTS.md	  4. Furthermore, §15.5 (line 2054) assumes that a single PCOC's legs are strictly sequential so that using `C` CPU cores requires running `C` distinct PCOCs with `C × 256 MiB` of separate terrains. Because a fake leg takes 0 steps to produce a valid `checkpoints[j]` reset point, an attacker with `C` cores sharing **one** 256 MiB terrain can insert `C - 1` fake legs in a long hike of `L` legs and compute the remaining `L - (C - 1)` honest legs **in parallel across all `C` cores**. For example, in a 2,000-leg hike on an 8-core machine, inserting 7 fake legs (`0.35%` fake fraction) lets all 8 cores walk honest legs in parallel on a single 256 MiB terrain while passing an 18-leg thorough draw `(1 - 7/2000)^18 = 93.9%` of the time (or `97.9%` of the time for §14 standalone `verify`, which only ever checks 6 legs).
